import Snippet from "../../../../components/docs/Snippet.astro";

The Node drop-in reads the device's license document from the `X-PKey-License` header, verifies it offline against your pinned keys and refuses the request when the license doesn't allow it. A route with no gate stays open. The contract is on [Verify licenses on your server](/docs/build/servers/).

Requires the License feature and the config file `pkey sdk --lang node --write` writes. The app sends `X-PKey-License` and `X-PKey-Device` with each call to your server.

## Steps

1. **Server** Install `@polaris-key/server` from Polaris Key's npm feed, and generate the config file with `pkey sdk --lang node --write`.
2. **Server** Build one `createNextPolarisKey({ config })` in a shared module and import it from each route.
3. **Server** Wrap each route handler in a gate: `requireLicense`, `requireEntitlement`, `requireTier` or `requireSignIn`.

<Snippet
  src="packages/shared-manifest/test/fixtures/integration/node/server/licensing.next.ts"
  title="app/api/pro/route.ts"
/>

A gated handler receives the request, then the license context, then Next's own route context with its params. To refuse before a route runs, export `polaris.middleware([...])` from `middleware.ts`: the first rule whose path matches decides, and a path no rule matches passes. The middleware can't hand the license to the route, so a route that reads it wraps its handler too; the verdict is cached, so it isn't verified twice.

## Require a signed-in account

`requireSignIn()` refuses with `sign_in_required` (403) while no account is signed in on the device. The handler's context has `user.subject`, the account's pairwise subject.

<Snippet
  src="packages/shared-manifest/test/fixtures/integration/node/server/identity.next.ts"
  title="app/api/me/route.ts"
/>
